Antony Blinken (born April 16, 1962) is an American lawyer and diplomat who served as the 71st United States secretary of state from 2021 to 2025.

Originally depicted as a lioness, this ancient Egyptian goddess was later associated with the domestic cat and worshipped as early as 2890 BCE, sharing a dual nature with the warrior goddess Sekhmet — who is she?
Bastet (Ancient), also known as Ubasti or Bubastis, is a goddess of ancient Egyptian religion, possibly of Nubian origin, worshipped as early as the Second Dynasty (2890 BCE).
Believed to have once been an NKVD informant, this Polish communist led his country from 1948 to 1956 and imposed the Stalinist system there — who was he?
Bolesław Bierut (18 April 1892 - 12 March 1956) was a Polish communist activist and politician who was the leader of communist-ruled Poland from 1948 until 1956.

Charles Cornwallis, 1st Marquess Cornwallis (31 December 1738 - 5 October 1805) was a British Army officer, Whig politician and colonial administrator.
This immensely wealthy final king of Lydia fell to Cyrus the Great after the fall of his capital, Sardis, in the 6th century BC — who was he?
Croesus (Ancient) was the last king of Lydia from 585 BC to 546 BC.

Dubbed the 'Father of the Nation' and also a noted historian behind the book Capitalism and Slavery, this leader steered Trinidad and Tobago to independence — who is it?
Eric Williams (25 September 1911 - 29 March 1981) was a Trinidad and Tobago politician.

This Dutch politician served as First Vice-President of the European Commission under Jean-Claude Juncker, later became the EU's climate action commissioner, and then led a Dutch political alliance in parliament from 2023 to 2025. Who is he?
Frans Timmermans (born 6 May 1961) is a Dutch politician who was the leader of GroenLinks-PvdA in the House of Representatives from 2023 to 2025.
Working alongside Simone de Beauvoir to expose torture during the Algerian War, this feminist lawyer later signed a landmark 1971 declaration demanding free abortion access — who is she?
Gisèle Halimi (born Zeiza Gisle lise Taeb,; 27 July 1927 - 28 July 2020) was a Tunisian-French lawyer, politician, essayist and feminist activist.
As China's top leader on Hong Kong and Macau affairs, this former Shanghai mayor rose to the Politburo Standing Committee before becoming vice president in 2023 — who is he?
Han Zheng (pinyin: Hn Zhng; born April 1955) is a Chinese politician who, since 2023, has served as the 11th vice president of China.

History of religion is the written record of human religious feelings, thoughts, and ideas.
A professor of Ukrainian language and a nationalist member of parliament from 2012 to 2014, this linguist campaigned hard for heritage-language learning - who is she?

Jeanine Pirro (born June 2, 1951) is a Lebanese-American television host, lawyer, and author who has been serving as the United States attorney for the District of Columbia since May 2025.
This Nova Scotian-born seaman turned his record-setting solo voyage aboard the Spray into the best-seller "Sailing Alone Around the World" — who was he?
Joshua Slocum (February 20, 1844 - on or shortly after November 14, 1909) was the first person to sail single-handedly around the world.
Commander of the Tobruk-based Libyan National Army, this officer has been the de facto ruler of eastern Libya since 2017, governing it as a military dictatorship. Who is he?
Khalifa Haftar (born 7 November 1943) is a Libyan politician, military officer, and the commander of the Tobruk-based Libyan National Army (LNA).
Born Lev Bronstein, this Marxist theorist stood with Lenin as one of the two most prominent figures of the early Soviet state — until he was exiled in 1929 and assassinated in 1940. Who was he?
Leon Trotsky was Soviet politician and revolutionary (1879–1940).
Chancellor of a university in Haryana and MLA for Tijara in Rajasthan, this politician also serves as the eighth head of a Hindu monastic sect — who is he?
Mahant Balaknath (born 16 April 1984) is an Indian politician and current MLA from Tijara constituency in Rajasthan.
This French politician has led the La France Insoumise parliamentary group in the National Assembly since 2021, having represented a Val-de-Marne constituency since 2017 — who is she?
Mathilde Panot (French; born 15 January 1989) is a French politician who has served as the president of the La France Insoumise group in the National Assembly since October 2021.
This Roman goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare shared the Capitoline Triad with Jupiter and Juno, and is often shown with an owl — who is she?
Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, justice, law, victory, and the sponsor of arts, trade, and strategy.
While 'nudism' stresses the practice itself, this near-synonym highlights an attitude of harmony with nature woven into non-sexual social nudity — which term?
Naturism is a lifestyle of practicing non-sexual social nudity in private and in public; the word also refers to the cultural movement which advocates and defends that lifestyle.
Marked by financial and personal failure before 1640, this English soldier rose to lead Parliament's army, championed the execution of Charles I, and ruled as Lord Protector. Who is he?
Oliver Cromwell (25 April 1599 - 3 September 1658) was an English statesman, farmer and soldier, widely regarded as one of the most important figures in British history.
This historical region in southwestern Iran, corresponding to Fars province, saw Iranic-speaking migrants arrive from Central Asia in ancient times — what is it called?
Persis is a historical region in south-western Iran, roughly corresponding with Fars province.

Officially known as the Religious Society of Friends, members of this Christian movement got their popular nickname after founder George Fox told a judge to 'quake before the authority of God' — what are they called?
Quakers are people who belong to the Religious Society of Friends, originally known as simply the Society of Friends, a historically Protestant Christian set of denominations.
A decorated Vietnam Marine awarded a Bronze Star and Purple Heart, he led the FBI as its sixth director from 2001 to 2013 after appointments under presidents of both parties. Who?
Robert Mueller (August 7, 1944 - March 20, 2026) was an American lawyer who served as the sixth director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) from 2001 to 2013.

United Arab Republic was a country and sovereign state in the Middle East from 1958 to 1971.

Nero: Roman emperor from AD 54 to 68.

The Exodus: Founding myth of the Jewish people.

What is the atomic number of Iodine?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
What is the atomic number of Cobalt?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
In what year was Albert Einstein born?
Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 – 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.
In what year was Andromeda Galaxy discovered?
Andromeda Galaxy: The Andromeda Galaxy is a barred spiral galaxy and is the nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way.
Pillars of Creation: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The astronomers responsible for the photo were Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen from Arizona State University.
Which company manufactures KAI T-50 Golden Eagle?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Korea Aerospace Industries. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
Which country is Yakovlev MC-21 based from?
Yakovlev MC-21: Russia. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Livermorium?
Livermorium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Who is credited with discovering Fentanyl?
Fentanyl: Paul Janssen. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.
Who is credited with discovering Arsenic?
Arsenic: Albertus Magnus. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
An economist who once worked for the IMF and later served as Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire from 1990 to 1993, this politician has been the country's president since 2010 — name this leader?
Alassane Ouattara (French; born 1 January 1942) is an Ivorian politician and economist who has been President of Ivory Coast (Cte d'Ivoire) since 2010.
Whether from too few red blood cells or faulty hemoglobin, this disorder leaves the blood less able to carry oxygen — often felt as quiet tiredness long before any paleness shows — what is it?
Anemia (also spelt anaemia in British English) is a blood disorder in which the blood has a reduced ability to carry oxygen.
Sharing chemistry with phosphorus and antimony, this group-15 metalloid carries the symbol As and a notorious reputation for toxicity — what is it?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.

This genus of deciduous trees includes 14 species across two subgenera, one found only in East Asia with low, multi-trunked growth, the other spanning Europe, Asia, and eastern North America. What tree genus is this?

Beech (genus Fagus) is a genus of deciduous trees in the family Fagaceae, native to subtropical (accessory forest element) and temperate (as dominant element of mesophytic forests) Eurasia and North America.
As Square's chief technology officer, this software engineer helped build Cash App before he was fatally stabbed in San Francisco in 2023 — who was he?
Bob Lee (businessman) (December 20, 1979 - April 4, 2023) was an American businessman and software engineer who was best known for helping to create the financial service Cash App.
Located between the lower back and the perineum, these two rounded regions of human anatomy are built around the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — name this body part?
Buttocks (sing.: buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of humans, located on the posterior of the pelvic region.
Portuguese explorers carried this tropical American tree to India in the 16th century; today Ivory Coast and India lead a 3.9-million-ton global harvest of its nut — what is it?
Cashew is the common name of a tropical evergreen tree Anacardium occidentale, in the family Anacardiaceae.
The first element in group 6, it lends its name to the shiny plating on car bumpers and, mixed into steel, makes it stainless. Which steely-grey metal is it?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
This bird's name comes from the Quechua word 'kuntur,' and its California-dwelling relative was nearly wiped out by habitat loss — which giant vulture soars over the Andes?
Condor is the common name for two genera of New World vultures, each with one extant species.
As of December 2025 worth an estimated $8.7 billion, this Swedish businessman founded and chairs a massive music-streaming company — who is he?
Daniel Ek (Swedish; born 21 February 1983) is a Swedish businessman and technologist.
Found in nighttime cold remedies like NyQuil and paired with vitamin B6 for pregnancy-related nausea, this antihistamine is an inverse agonist at the H1 receptor — which drug?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine medication used to treat insomnia and allergies, and - in combination with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - to treat morning sickness in pregnant women.
This inner lining of the uterus thickens each cycle and is shed during menstruation in humans and a handful of other species, including certain bats and shrews — what is it?
Endometrium is the inner lining of the uterus (womb) in mammals.
Cats in this subfamily can purr but never roar, thanks to a bony rather than flexible hyoid bone — which subfamily?
Felinae are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.

A French economist who gave lectures up and down the country and helped found the Inter-Parliamentary Union, he shared the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901 for his work in Europe's peace movement — who was he?
Frédéric Passy (20 May 1822 - 12 June 1912) was a French economist and pacifist who was a founding member of several peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
This week-long 2010 manhunt across Tyne and Wear and Northumberland ended when the fugitive shot himself following a six-hour standoff near Rothbury. What event is it?
Goose (pl.: geese) is a bird of any of several waterfowl species in the family Anatidae.

Linked to conditions like tuberculosis, bronchitis, and lung cancer, this medical term describes blood discharged from the airway rather than internal bleeding elsewhere in the body. What is it called?
Hemoptysis is the discharge of blood or blood-stained mucus through the mouth coming from the bronchi, larynx, trachea, or lungs.
This negatively charged ion, one oxygen bonded to one hydrogen, acts as a base and forms industrially vital salts like the sodium version used to make millions of tons of chemicals. What ion is it?
Hydroxide (occasionally hydroxyl ion) is a diatomic anion with chemical formula OH.
One of the largest dog breeds in the world, this sighthound was historically used to course game and became the official mascot of a British Guards regiment in 1902. What breed is it?
Irish Wolfhound is a breed of large sighthound that has, by its presence and substantial size, inspired literature, poetry and mythology.
This Johns Hopkins psychologist coined the terms 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' and believed gender was malleable during a child's first two years. Who was he?
John Money (8 July 1921 - 7 July 2006) was a New Zealand American psychologist, sexologist and professor at Johns Hopkins University known for his research on human sexual behavior and gender.
These paired folds of skin are the major externally visible structures of the vulva, with an outer 'majora' set and an inner 'minora' set — what are they called?
Labia are the major externally visible structures of the vulva. In other mammals, the labia majora are not present and the labia minora are instead referred to as the labia vulvae.

The second woman to earn a physics doctorate from the University of Vienna, this Austrian-Swedish scientist became the first female full physics professor in Germany — and was instrumental in discovering nuclear fission. Who is she?
Lise Meitner (7 November 1878 - 27 October 1968) was an Austrian and Swedish nuclear physicist who was instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission.

Made by every living organism and responsible for much of the sour taste in fruit, this dicarboxylic food additive's salt form also serves as a key intermediate in the cell's central metabolic energy cycle — what compound is it?
Malic acid is an organic compound with the molecular formula HO2CCH(OH)CH2CO2H.

This mammal family, uniting skunks and stink badgers, is defined by highly developed scent glands used to ward off predators, and was only split from the weasel family in the 1990s — what family is it?
Mephitidae is a family of mammals comprising the skunks and stink badgers.
This unique group of mammals is the only one whose members lay eggs rather than bear live young, comprising the platypus and four echidna species — what group is it?
Monotreme are mammals of the order Monotremata.

First arising in wormlike creatures some 550 million years ago, this body-wide network coordinates actions and relays sensory signals through a central half and a peripheral half — what system is being described?
Nervous system is the highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body.
Beginning in the embryo and maturing a primary oocyte into a fertilization-ready egg cell, what is this reproductive process called?
Oogenesis is the differentiation of the ovum (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
Native to the islands of Southeast Asia, this bushy perennial herb in the mint family is prized for a fragrant essential oil used widely in perfumery — what plant is it?
Patchouli (also spelled patchouly or pachouli; Pogostemon cablin) is a species of flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, commonly called the mint or deadnettle family.

First described in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the cellar spider and the "vibrating spider" — and lends the nickname "daddy long-legs" to one of its species; what is the family?
Pholcidae are a family of araneomorph spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.
Native to Southeast Asia and a natural, non-hybrid ancestor of both the grapefruit and the bitter orange, this largest of all citrus fruits also goes by the name 'shaddock' — what is it?
Pomelo (PUM-; or pummelo, Citrus maxima), also known as a shaddock, is the largest citrus fruit.
This opening at the center of the iris lets light reach the retina and appears black — round in people, a slit in cats, and even a ring shape in some catfish — what's it called?
Pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
Named from Greek words for 'rose' and 'tree,' this genus of over 1,000 woody flowering plant species serves as the national flower of Nepal and the state flower of Washington — what is it?

Rhododendron (pl.: rhododendra), from Ancient Greek (rhdon), meaning "rose", and (dndron), meaning "tree", is a very large genus of about 1,024 species of woody plants in the heath family (Ericaceae).
The FAO/WHO Codex standard recognizes 21 species under this common name for small silvery forage fish, distinguished from their larger 'pilchard' cousins mainly by size — what fish is it?
Sardine are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei.

Developed by the Chukchi people in the Russian Far East for pulling sleds and companionship, this medium-sized Spitz-family dog breed is smaller than the similar-looking Alaskan Malamute — name the breed?
Siberian Husky is a breed of medium-sized working sled dog.
The largest order of reptiles, this group is set apart by movable quadrate bones that let snakes gape their jaws around oversized prey — what's the order called?
Squamata (Latin squamatus, 'scaly, having scales') is the largest order of reptiles; most members of which are commonly known as lizards, with the group also including snakes.

This medical term describes a resting heart rate above 100 beats per minute in adults, which can be either a normal exercise response or a sign of an electrical problem in the heart — what's the condition called?
Tachycardia is a heart rate that exceeds the normal resting rate.
This viral brain infection, transmitted through the bite of infected parasitic arachnids, saw its European case count climb almost 400% over three decades. What is this arachnid-spread illness?
Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.
With 92 protons and half-lives stretching up to 4.5 billion years, this radioactive metal is handy for dating the age of the Earth — which silvery-grey element?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
His 1925 Umdeutung paper reinterpreted old quantum theory, and two years later he published a famous uncertainty principle — which German physicist was he?

Werner Heisenberg (5 December 1901 - 1 February 1976) was a German theoretical physicist, one of the main pioneers of the theory of quantum mechanics and a principal scientist in the German nuclear program during World War II.
Named for its standard passenger capacity, this twin-engine turboprop regional airliner is assembled in Toulouse by a Franco-Italian manufacturer that is half-owned by Airbus — what aircraft is this?
ATR 72: Regional turboprop airliner. The ATR 72 is a twin-engine turboprop, short-haul regional airliner developed and produced in France and Italy by aircraft manufacturer ATR.
Sold as button, cremini, or portobello depending on its stage of maturity, this cultivated mushroom is grown in more than 70 countries — what species is it?
Agaricus bisporus: Species of fungus. Agaricus bisporus, commonly known as the cultivated mushroom, is a basidiomycete mushroom native to grasslands in Eurasia and North America.
Meaning 'different lizard' and first described in 1877 by Othniel Marsh, most fossils of this Late Jurassic predator come from North America's Morrison Formation — which dinosaur?
This Manchester physicist shared the 2010 Nobel Prize for his work on graphene — and is the only person to also hold an Ig Nobel, won for levitating a frog with magnetism. Who is he?
The average adult sheds 50 to 70 billion cells a day through this tidy, programmed cell death — named from a Greek word for 'falling off' — quite unlike messy, traumatic necrosis. What is it?
Apoptosis: Form of programmed cell death. Because apoptosis cannot stop once it has begun, it is a highly regulated process.
Driven by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease builds plaque lesions inside artery walls and can lead to stroke or coronary trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis: Inflammatory disease involving a buildup of lesions in the walls of arteries.

Developed in the 18th century by an English clergyman and, independently, by Pierre-Simon Laplace, this rule lets you flip a conditional probability — say, finding the odds a patient is sick given a positive test. What is it?
Bayes' theorem: Mathematical rule for inverting probabilities.
Colloquially called a buffalo in the US and Canada, this large bovine is actually more closely related to yaks and cattle than to true buffalo — which animal?
Hailing from the Anglo-Scottish frontier and frequently cited as the most intelligent dog breed on Earth, which sheepdog dominates sheepdog trials?
Border Collie: Working dog breed. The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size.
Encompassing reporting, dashboards, data mining, and analytics, this set of strategies and technologies helps companies turn raw data into strategic decisions — what's it called?
Business intelligence: Strategies for analysis and use of data.
Domesticated in Mexico roughly 6,000 years ago, this nightshade produces berries used in cooking, medicine, and even self-defense sprays — which plant species is it?
Capsicum annuum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Originally called 'centigrade' from Latin words for a hundred and steps, this SI temperature scale was renamed in 1948 to honor the Swedish astronomer who proposed it in 1742 — which scale?
Celsius: Unit of measurement for temperature.

The second-lightest halogen, this yellow-green gas is so reactive it has the highest electron affinity of any element and once fascinated medieval alchemists heating chloride salts — which element is it?
Chlorine: Chemical element with atomic number 17 (Cl)
Native to the Americas from Mexico to South America, this diurnal member of the Procyonidae family goes by the name 'quash' in Belize — what is it?

Known to NATO by the reporting name 'Mop' and to Canadian forces as the Canso, this WWII flying boat served every branch of the U.S. military and remained in some air forces into the 1980s — which aircraft?
Consolidated PBY Catalina: American 1930s flying boat.
Native to the Irano-Turanian region, this flowering plant's dried seeds season cuisines worldwide, despite no strong evidence backing its use in traditional medicine — which spice?
Cumin: Species of plant with seeds used as a spice.
This field statistically studies human populations — their size and makeup — through the interplay of births, deaths, and migration — what is it?
Demography: Study of human populations and their structures.
Descended from the African wild ass and domesticated some 5,000 to 7,000 years ago, which working equine still numbers over 40 million worldwide?
Donkey: Domesticated animal primarily used for transportation.
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
Also known as the bodhi tree, this species is revered in four South Asian religions as the tree beneath which Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment — which species?
Ficus religiosa: Species of fig. Ficus religiosa or sacred fig is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?

Germany's first professor of experimental physics is remembered both for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him and for the witty posthumous notebooks he called "waste books" — who was he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg: German scientist and satirist (1742–1799)
This plant genus in the mallow family gives us cotton, humanity's primary natural fiber, with its name tracing to an Arabic word for a soft substance — which genus?
Gossypium: Genus of flowering plants in the mallow family Malvaceae.

Derived independently in the 1830s by two European researchers and later given theoretical backing by George Stokes, this law describes the pressure drop of laminar flow through a drinking straw or a hypodermic needle — what's it called?
Hagen–Poiseuille equation: Law describing the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid.
Nicknamed for its shaggy white spines that dangle over a centimeter long, this edible mushroom is commonly called lion's mane and is used in traditional Chinese medicine — which fungus?
Hericium erinaceus: Edible mushroom. Hericium erinaceus, commonly known as lion's mane, yamabushitake, bearded tooth fungus, or bearded hedgehog, is a species of tooth fungus.
This climbing, hemp-family plant's female cone-shaped flowers are used to flavor and preserve beer — what's the scientific name for hops?
Humulus lupulus: Species of flowering plant.
Roche once used up to 90% of the world's crop of this star-shaped spice to manufacture the flu drug Tamiflu via shikimic acid — what is it?
Illicium verum: Star anise, an evergreen tree.
The largest tree fruit on Earth can hit 120 pounds and 35 inches long — a 'multiple fruit' made of thousands of individual flowers, with a single tree bearing hundreds a year. What is it?
On January 26, 1926, this Scottish inventor gave the world's first demonstration of a working mechanical television system — who is he?
With an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters and a record of 5.85 meters, this snake is the world's longest venomous species, endemic to Asia. What is it?
King cobra: Group of venomous snakes from Asia.
Spread through the bite of sandflies, this parasitic disease can appear in cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral forms, the last marked by fever and an enlarged spleen — what is it called?
Leishmaniasis: Disease caused by parasites of the Leishmania type.

This anatomic form of lung infection causes inflammatory fluid to consolidate across an entire continuous section of one lung, and in children shows up instead as a rounded pattern due to immature air-pore connections — what is it?
Lobar pneumonia: Lung infection. It is one of three anatomic classifications of pneumonia (the other being bronchopneumonia and atypical pneumonia).
A field of artificial intelligence built on statistics and optimization, it develops algorithms that learn from data and handle unseen examples without being explicitly programmed — what is it?
Machine learning: Subset of artificial intelligence. Statistics and mathematical optimisation methods compose the foundations of machine learning.

In 1835 this Scottish polymath and Caroline Herschel became the first female Honorary Members of the Royal Astronomical Society, and she signed first on John Stuart Mill's 1866 petition for women's suffrage — who was she?
Patented in 1922 and later marketed as Novalgin or Analgin, this painkiller's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare blood-cell risk called agranulocytosis — what is it?
Metamizole: Medication. Metamizole or dipyrone is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
Normally equal to 60 seconds, which unit of time has occasionally run 61 seconds long in UTC due to leap seconds, though a 59-second version has never actually occurred?
Minute: Unit of time equal to 60 seconds. The prime symbol ′ is also sometimes used informally to denote minutes.
Nicknamed the barking deer for its unusual call, this small Asian deer genus has fossils dating back as far as 35 million years — what is it?
This general term describes inflammation of the kidneys, affecting structures such as the glomeruli, tubules, or the surrounding interstitial tissue — what is the condition called?
Nephritis: Inflammation of the kidneys. It is one of several different types of nephropathy.
The largest structure inside a eukaryotic cell's nucleus, this site of ribosome assembly also helps form signal recognition particles and responds to cellular stress — what is it?
Nucleolus: Largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. The nucleolus also participates in the formation of signal recognition particles and plays a role in the cell's response to stress.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this degenerative joint disease comes from the breakdown of cartilage and bone, often striking the fingertips, thumb base, knees, and hips — what is it?
Osteoarthritis: Form of arthritis caused by degeneration of joints.

Also called the blue passionflower, this South American vine climbs via tendrils to 10 metres, bears fragrant blue-white blooms with a fringed coronal filament, and produces an edible but not particularly tasty orange fruit — which plant is it?
Passiflora caerulea: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.
Usually caused by a virus but sometimes by strep bacteria, this inflammation of the back of the throat brings on a sore throat, fever, and sometimes a hoarse voice — what is it called?
Pharyngitis: Inflammation of the back of the throat. Pharyngitis is a type of upper respiratory tract infection.
Connected to the fetus by the umbilical cord, this temporary organ handles nutrient and waste exchange between mother and baby during pregnancy — what is it?
Placenta: Organ that connects the fetus to the uterine wall.
Despite its common name, this burrowing rodent native to North American grasslands is actually a type of ground squirrel, not a canine — what is it?
Prairie dog: Genus of ground squirrels.
Ranging from Penguin Random House to countless small independent players, which broad industry covers making books, magazines, music, and software available to the public, in print or digital form?
Publishing: Production and distribution of media.

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?
When an infection-triggered immune overreaction sends blood pressure plummeting and disrupts cells throughout the body, doctors in the ICU are treating this life-threatening condition — what is it?
Septic shock: Dangerously low blood pressure due to damage from an organ infection.

Its last natural case appeared in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared it the only human disease ever wiped off the Earth — which scourge, known for fluid-filled blisters that scarred survivors, was it?
Commonly nicknamed phlegm, this mucus coughed up from the trachea and bronchi is examined for tell-tale yellow or green coloring that signals infection — what is it?
Sputum: Mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways.

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
Predicted by Mendeleev decades before its discovery and sitting in the periodic table between manganese and rhenium, what is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive?
Technetium: Chemical element with atomic number 43 (Tc)
Native to the Mediterranean and a member of the mint family Lamiaceae, this dried herb's most common culinary variety, Thymus vulgaris, hails from Southeast Europe — what is it?
Thyme: Culinary herb. Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
Triceratops: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur.

Known by names like lingonberry and cowberry, this evergreen shrub's tart berries are a Nordic cuisine staple and are commercially grown in the Pacific Northwest and the Netherlands — what is its scientific name?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea: Species of shrub with edible fruit.
Descended from a wild bovine ancestor, this large domesticated animal from the Indian subcontinent now also grazes fields in Italy, the Balkans, and Australia — what is it?
Water buffalo: Species of large bovine. The wild water buffalo (Bubalus arnee) is most probably the ancestor of the domestic water buffalo.
Based on how long Earth takes to orbit the Sun, this unit of time comes in tropical and sidereal forms differing by about 20 minutes, with leap years keeping our calendar in sync — what unit?

Year: Unit of time based on Earth's orbit. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.

What is the chemical symbol for nickel?
The symbol for nickel is Ni. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.

Ryan O'Neal: Charles Patrick Ryan O'Neal (April 20, 1941 – December 8, 2023) was an American actor.
